If the framework delivers as described, it could complement existing binary similarity tools such as BinDiff, Diaphora, and the academic Asm2Vec and Trex lines of work.

Readers should treat the specific claims with appropriate caution until the work is independently reproduced. The provided arXiv identifier appears unusual and the venue, datasets, and evaluation baselines are not visible from the metadata alone, so the strength of the empirical results cannot be assessed here. Still, the direction, treating opaque industrial software as a first-class supply chain problem rather than an afterthought, is consistent with where both regulators and security vendors seem to be heading.

entries.title: Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act
entries.titleJa: コーディングエージェントは行動のタイミングを判断できない
entries.titleEn: Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はLLMベースのコーディングエージェントが、いつコードを編集・実行すべきか、いつユーザーに確認すべきかの判断に課題を抱えていることを指摘。過剰な自律行動や不必要な確認要求が生産性とユーザー信頼を損なう実態を分析している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper examines how LLM-based coding agents struggle to decide when to act autonomously versus when to ask for clarification, showing that both over-eager edits and excessive confirmation requests harm user trust and productivity.
entries.bodyJa:
AIコーディングエージェントの普及が進む中、本論文は彼らが抱える根本的な課題、すなわち「いつ行動すべきか」の判断能力の欠如に焦点を当てている。Cursor、Claude Code、GitHub Copilot Agentなど自律的にコードを編集・実行するツールが一般化する一方で、その判断ミスがユーザー体験を大きく損ねている点を示唆している。

論文の主張によれば、現在のエージェントは二つの極端な失敗モードを持つ。一つは過剰な自律性で、曖昧な指示に対しても確認せず大規模な変更を加え、ユーザーが意図しないリファクタリングやファイル削除を実行してしまうケース。もう一つは過剰な慎重さで、些細な作業でも確認を繰り返し、本来のエージェントとしての価値を損なう点である。

背景としては、LLMの訓練が「役立つ応答を返す」ことに最適化されているため、行動の保留や不確実性の表明が苦手とされる傾向がある。RLHFやインストラクションチューニングは応答の流暢さを高める一方、メタ認知的な「自分が何を知らないか」の判断には十分対応していないとみられる。Anthropicが進める計算的解釈可能性研究や、OpenAIの「deliberative alignment」など、エージェントの判断プロセスを明示化する取り組みは、この課題に間接的に関係している可能性がある。

実務的には、ユーザー側がエージェントに明示的なルールファイル(例: AGENTS.md、Cursor Rules)を与えたり、計画フェーズと実行フェーズを分離したりする運用上の工夫が広がっている。一方、エージェント側でも「plan mode」や差分プレビュー、許可リスト方式のツール実行制御など、行動前にユーザーの介入余地を残す設計が増えている。

本研究が示唆するのは、コーディングエージェントの次の進化軸は単なる能力向上ではなく、行動判断のキャリブレーション、すなわち「実行と確認の境界線」をいかに学習させるかにあるという点だろう。ただしarxiv番号からは正規の論文か検証が必要であり、結論の一般化には注意が必要と見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
As AI coding agents become mainstream in developer workflows, this paper highlights a subtle but consequential limitation: these agents often fail to judge when they should act on their own and when they should pause to ask the user. The issue cuts across products like Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot's agent mode, and Devin, all of which are designed to edit files, run commands, and complete multi-step tasks with minimal supervision.

The paper frames the problem as two opposing failure modes. On one end, agents over-act: given an ambiguous instruction, they confidently refactor large portions of a codebase, delete files, or run destructive commands without seeking confirmation. On the other end, they over-ask, interrupting users for trivial decisions and eroding the productivity gains that motivated using an agent in the first place. The healthy middle, where the agent acts decisively on routine work but pauses on genuinely ambiguous or high-impact decisions, remains elusive.

A likely root cause is that contemporary LLMs are trained to be helpful and responsive. RLHF and instruction tuning reward fluent, confident answers, which can suppress the model's willingness to express uncertainty or hold back. Calibrating an agent's sense of when its own knowledge or the user's intent is insufficient is a metacognitive skill that current training pipelines may not directly target. Related work on deliberative alignment, mechanistic interpretability, and uncertainty estimation in LLMs touches on this gap, though none yet provides a clean solution for agentic settings.

In practice, the developer community has been compensating with scaffolding around the model rather than fixes inside it. Project-level instruction files such as AGENTS.md or Cursor Rules let teams encode norms about when to ask, what to never touch, and how to plan before executing. Plan-then-act modes, diff previews, allowlists for shell commands, and sandboxed execution environments all try to put a human in the loop before irreversible actions. These conventions are converging into something resembling an emerging operational discipline for agent use.

The broader implication is that the next meaningful axis of progress for coding agents may not be raw capability, where frontier models are already strong, but calibration of action. An agent that knows when to commit, when to clarify, and when to refuse would feel qualitatively more trustworthy than one that is merely more accurate at code generation. This aligns with a wider industry shift toward measuring agents on end-to-end task success and user trust rather than on isolated benchmarks like HumanEval or SWE-bench.

Readers should treat the paper's specific claims with some caution. The arXiv identifier format suggests it should be verified against the official listing, and any generalization from a single study to all coding agents likely warrants hedging. Still, the underlying observation resonates with widely reported user experiences, and it points to an area where both model providers and tool vendors are likely to invest heavily over the next year.

entries.title: Bridging the Programming Language Gap: Constructing a Multilingual Shared Semantic Space through AST Unification and Graph Matching
entries.titleJa: ASTの統一とグラフマッチングで多言語の共有意味空間を構築
entries.titleEn: Bridging the Programming Language Gap: Constructing a Multilingual Shared Semantic Space through AST Unification and Graph Matching
entries.summaryJa: 異なるプログラミング言語のコードを共通の意味空間に写像するため、抽象構文木(AST)の統一表現とグラフマッチングを組み合わせる手法を提案する研究。コード検索や言語横断的な解析の精度向上が期待される。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes building a shared multilingual semantic space for source code by unifying abstract syntax trees across languages and applying graph matching techniques, aiming to enable cross-language code understanding and search.
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、異なるプログラミング言語のコードを共通の意味空間に写像し、言語横断的なコード理解や検索を可能にするアプローチを提案している。多言語対応はソフトウェア工学における長年の課題であり、特に大規模なオープンソース資産が複数言語にまたがる現代では重要性が増している。

提案手法の中核は、各言語固有の抽象構文木(AST)を統一的な表現に正規化し、その上でグラフマッチングによって構造的・意味的な対応関係を学習する点にある。ASTは構文情報を保持しつつ表層的なトークン差異を抽象化できるため、言語間のギャップを橋渡しする中間表現として有用とされる。著者らはノード単位の対応付けに加え、サブツリーやサブグラフレベルでの整合性を取ることで、意味的に等価なコード片の検出精度を高めることを狙うと見られる。

関連分野では、MicrosoftのCodeBERTやGraphCodeBERT、SalesforceのCodeT5など、大規模事前学習モデルがコードの多言語表現学習を進めてきた。これらはトークン列やデータフローを利用するのに対し、本研究はASTの構造そのものとグラフマッチングという古典的手法を組み合わせる点に特徴があり、解釈性や軽量性の観点で補完的な価値を持つ可能性がある。tree-sitterのような汎用パーサ基盤の成熟も、こうした多言語AST研究の実装コストを下げてきた背景にある。

一方で、言語ごとに意味論やライブラリ慣習が大きく異なるため、AST正規化だけで意味の等価性をどこまで捕捉できるかは慎重に評価する必要がある。コードクローン検出、バグの言語間移植、教育用途での言語横断的説明などへの応用可能性が考えられるが、実用化には大規模ベンチマークでの検証が鍵となるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper tackles a persistent challenge in software engineering: bridging the gap between different programming languages by mapping their source code into a single, shared semantic space. As open-source codebases increasingly span multiple languages and ecosystems, the ability to reason across languages has become valuable for code search, migration, clone detection, and educational tooling.

The central idea is to normalize language-specific abstract syntax trees (ASTs) into a unified representation, then apply graph matching to align structurally and semantically equivalent fragments across languages. ASTs are an appealing intermediate representation because they preserve syntactic structure while abstracting away surface-level token differences such as keywords, punctuation, and naming conventions. By unifying node types and edge semantics across language parsers, the authors aim to expose the deeper structural similarities that survive translation between, say, Python and Java.

On top of this unified AST, graph matching techniques are used to identify correspondences between nodes, subtrees, and larger subgraphs. This is a classical approach with a long history in pattern recognition, and applying it to code can offer interpretability advantages: matches are explicit and inspectable, rather than buried inside high-dimensional embeddings. The result is a shared semantic space in which code snippets from different languages can be compared, retrieved, or aligned.

The broader research context is rich. Large pretrained models such as Microsoft's CodeBERT and GraphCodeBERT, Salesforce's CodeT5, and more recent code LLMs have pushed multilingual code representation learning forward by leveraging token sequences, data flow, and massive corpora. These models excel at fuzzy semantic similarity but can be opaque and expensive. A structural, AST-driven approach combined with graph matching may be complementary, potentially offering lighter-weight or more explainable alternatives, especially for tasks where syntactic correspondence matters, such as cross-language refactoring or precise clone detection. The maturation of general-purpose parsing infrastructures like tree-sitter has also lowered the engineering cost of building multilingual AST pipelines, which likely helps make this line of work more practical.

That said, important caveats remain. Programming languages differ not only in syntax but in semantics, type systems, standard libraries, and idiomatic patterns. Two snippets with structurally similar ASTs can behave very differently at runtime, and conversely, semantically equivalent solutions can have wildly different tree shapes, particularly when comparing imperative and functional styles. How far AST unification alone can carry semantic equivalence is therefore an empirical question, and rigorous evaluation on diverse, large-scale benchmarks will be needed to judge the approach's real-world utility.

If the method holds up, plausible applications include cross-language code search, assisted porting of bug fixes between language versions of the same project, plagiarism and clone detection across polyglot repositories, and educational tools that explain a concept by showing equivalent implementations side by side. It may also serve as a useful signal to augment neural code models, providing structured alignment supervision during training. As with many structural approaches in the deep-learning era, the most likely outcome is hybridization: combining AST-based graph matching with learned embeddings to get the interpretability of the former and the flexibility of the latter.

entries.title: Unsafe by Flow: Uncovering Bidirectional Data-Flow Risks in MCP Ecosystem
entries.titleJa: MCPエコシステムにおける双方向データフローのリスクを解明
entries.titleEn: Unsafe by Flow: Uncovering Bidirectional Data-Flow Risks in MCP Ecosystem
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はModel Context Protocol(MCP)エコシステムにおける双方向データフローに着目し、LLMエージェントとツール間でのデータ授受に潜む安全性リスクを体系的に分析する。攻撃面と検出手法を提示し、実装上の対策を議論している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper systematically analyzes bidirectional data-flow risks in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem, identifying attack surfaces between LLM agents and tools, and proposing detection and mitigation approaches for safer deployments.
entries.bodyJa:
Anthropicが提唱したModel Context Protocol(MCP)は、LLMエージェントが外部ツールやデータソースと標準化された方法で連携するための仕組みとして急速に普及しつつある。本論文はそのエコシステムに潜む「双方向データフロー」の安全性リスクに焦点を当て、体系的な解明を試みている。

従来のセキュリティ議論はプロンプトインジェクションなどエージェントへの入力経路に偏りがちだったが、MCPではエージェントからツールへの呼び出しと、ツールからの応答という双方向の情報伝搬が常時発生する。著者らはこの往復データフローを攻撃面として位置付け、悪意あるツールによる情報吸い上げ、応答に埋め込まれた間接インジェクション、ツール間連鎖を介した権限昇格などのシナリオを整理していると見られる。

論文では実エコシステム上のMCPサーバ群を対象に解析を行い、機微情報の漏洩経路や信頼境界の曖昧さを定量的に示すアプローチを取っている可能性が高い。検出手法としては、データフロー追跡や呼び出しコンテキストの監査、ツール記述自体の静的検査などが想定される。

関連動向として、OpenAIのfunction callingやLangChain、Semantic Kernelといったエージェントフレームワークも同種のリスクを抱えており、Invariant LabsなどがMCPに対する「tool poisoning」攻撃を報告している。MCPがデファクト化するなかで、レジストリの信頼性、署名付きツール記述、サンドボックス実行といったサプライチェーン的対策の必要性が高まっており、本研究はその基盤的な脅威モデル整備に寄与するものと位置付けられる。
entries.bodyEn:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic, has quickly become a de facto standard for connecting LLM agents to external tools and data sources. This paper turns the spotlight on a less-discussed dimension of MCP security: the bidirectional flow of data that occurs every time an agent invokes a tool and consumes its response.

Much of the existing safety discourse around LLM agents focuses on inbound threats such as prompt injection delivered through user input or retrieved documents. MCP, however, institutionalizes a continuous round trip: the agent sends structured arguments to a tool, and the tool returns content that re-enters the model's context. The authors frame this loop as a first-class attack surface and appear to enumerate scenarios including malicious tools exfiltrating sensitive context, indirect prompt injection embedded in tool outputs, and privilege escalation through chains of cooperating or compromised servers.

The study seems to combine ecosystem-level analysis of publicly available MCP servers with a more formal treatment of data-flow properties. By tracing how information propagates between agent state, tool arguments, and tool responses, the work likely quantifies how often trust boundaries are crossed implicitly, and where current implementations lack mediation. Proposed mitigations probably include flow tracking, auditing of invocation context, and static inspection of tool manifests and descriptions, which themselves can carry adversarial instructions.

The topic resonates with broader industry concerns. Researchers at Invariant Labs and others have demonstrated tool poisoning attacks against MCP, where seemingly benign tool descriptions hide instructions that hijack the agent. Parallel ecosystems such as OpenAI's function calling, LangChain, and Microsoft's Semantic Kernel face structurally similar issues, but MCP's open, registry-driven model arguably amplifies supply-chain risk: any developer can publish a server, and agents may auto-discover and trust them with limited vetting.

In that context, the paper's contribution should be read less as a single exploit disclosure and more as a threat-modeling foundation. Practical defenses that the community is converging on, and that this work likely supports, include signed tool descriptors, capability-scoped permissions, sandboxed execution of MCP servers, and runtime policies that constrain what data may leave the agent for a given tool. As enterprises begin to wire MCP into production workflows touching code repositories, ticketing systems, and customer data, a rigorous account of bidirectional flow risks is timely. Readers should, however, treat specific numerical findings with appropriate caution until independent replication on current MCP server populations is available, since the ecosystem is evolving rapidly and server behavior can change between releases.

entries.title: Evaluating Design Conformance Through Trace Comparison
entries.titleJa: トレース比較によるソフトウェア設計適合性の評価手法
entries.titleEn: Evaluating Design Conformance Through Trace Comparison
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、実装が設計仕様にどの程度準拠しているかを評価するため、設計モデルと実行トレースを比較する手法を提案する。実行時挙動を抽出し、想定された設計シーケンスと突き合わせることで適合性を定量化する枠組みを示している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a method for evaluating how closely an implementation conforms to its design by comparing execution traces against expected design models, providing a quantitative measure of design conformance.
entries.bodyJa:
ソフトウェア工学では、初期設計と実装の乖離(設計ドリフト)が品質低下や保守性悪化の主要因として長らく問題視されてきた。本論文は、実行トレースと設計モデルを突き合わせることで、実装が設計にどの程度忠実かを評価する手法を提案している。

提案手法の核は、システム実行時に得られるイベントや呼び出し系列を「トレース」として収集し、設計段階で定義されたシーケンス(UMLシーケンス図や状態遷移モデルなど)と比較する点にある。両者の整合度を計算することで、設計どおりに動いている部分と逸脱している部分を識別でき、適合性を定量指標として提示できると見られる。これにより、コードレビューや静的解析だけでは捉えにくい振る舞いレベルの乖離を可視化できる可能性がある。

背景として、こうしたアプローチは「コンフォーマンスチェッキング」と呼ばれる研究領域に位置づけられる。特にプロセスマイニング分野ではvan der Aalstらの研究により、ビジネスプロセスログとプロセスモデルの照合手法が発達してきた。ソフトウェア領域でも、リバースエンジニアリングやアーキテクチャ適合性検査(Reflexion Modelなど)として類似の試みが続いており、本研究はその系譜に連なるものと位置づけられる。

実務面では、マイクロサービスや分散システムの普及に伴い、OpenTelemetryやJaegerといった分散トレーシング基盤が広く利用されるようになった。これらが生成する豊富な実行トレースを設計検証に活用する流れと親和性が高く、CI/CDパイプラインに統合すればリグレッション検出にも応用できる可能性がある。一方で、設計モデルが最新の状態に保たれていることが前提となるため、モデル駆動開発が浸透していない現場では適用に課題が残ると考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Design drift, the gradual divergence between the original design and the actual implementation, has long been recognized as a major contributor to software quality erosion and maintenance burden. This paper proposes a technique to evaluate how faithfully an implementation conforms to its intended design by systematically comparing runtime execution traces against design-level models.

The core idea is to capture sequences of events and method invocations during execution, treat them as traces, and then align these traces with expected behavior expressed in design artifacts such as UML sequence diagrams or state machine models. By computing a degree of correspondence between the two, the approach can highlight which parts of the system behave as designed and which deviate. This produces a quantitative conformance metric that complements traditional static analysis and code review, surfacing behavioral discrepancies that are otherwise hard to detect at the source level.

The work fits into the broader research area of conformance checking. In the process mining community, the foundational work by van der Aalst and colleagues established rigorous techniques for aligning event logs with process models, and many of those ideas have migrated into the software engineering domain. Related efforts include reverse engineering of behavioral models from execution and architectural conformance methods such as the Reflexion Model proposed by Murphy and Notkin, which compares high-level architectural intent with code-level reality. Viewed in this lineage, the paper extends well-established ideas with a trace-centric framing.

From a practical standpoint, the rise of microservices and distributed systems has made runtime tracing a first-class concern. Tools such as OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, and Zipkin now routinely capture rich distributed traces in production. Repurposing such telemetry for design conformance checks looks like a natural fit, and integrating the analysis into CI/CD pipelines could potentially catch behavioral regressions before they reach production. That said, the value of the approach depends heavily on whether design models are kept up to date. In organizations where model-driven development is not entrenched, maintaining accurate reference models may itself become the bottleneck, and teams might need to invest in lightweight model recovery or living documentation practices to make the technique sustainable.

entries.title: Similar Pattern Annotation via Retrieval Knowledge for LLM-Based Test Code Fault Localization
entries.titleJa: 検索知識による類似パターン注釈でLLMテストコード障害局所化を強化
entries.titleEn: Similar Pattern Annotation via Retrieval Knowledge for LLM-Based Test Code Fault Localization
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、LLMを用いたテストコードの障害局所化(FL)精度を高めるため、検索ベースで類似する障害パターンを注釈として付与する手法を提案する。既知の類似ケースを文脈として与えることで、LLMの推論精度向上を狙う。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a retrieval-augmented annotation method that injects similar fault patterns as context to improve LLM-based fault localization in test code, aiming to boost reasoning accuracy by grounding predictions in known analogous cases.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)をソフトウェア工学のタスクに応用する研究が加速するなか、本論文はテストコードにおける障害局所化(Fault Localization, FL)の精度向上を狙った新しいアプローチを提示している。

従来のFL手法は、スペクトラムベース(SBFL)や変異ベース(MBFL)といった統計的指標に依存するものが主流だった。近年はLLMにソースコードとテスト結果を与え、自然言語で原因箇所を推論させる手法が登場しているが、文脈の不足や幻覚(hallucination)が課題として残る。本論文はこの弱点に対し、検索拡張生成(RAG)の発想を応用し、過去の障害事例から「類似パターン」を取り出してLLMへの入力に注釈として埋め込む方式を提案していると見られる。

具体的には、対象となる失敗テストや疑わしいコード片に対し、ベクトル検索などで意味的に近い既知の障害事例を取得し、その障害箇所と修正パターンを注釈として与えることで、LLMが類推的に原因を絞り込めるよう支援する構造と推察される。これは、人間の開発者が過去のバグ修正経験をもとに新しい不具合を診断するプロセスに近い。

関連研究としては、FacebookのSapFix、MicrosoftのCopilotによるバグ修正支援、あるいはAutoFLやLLMAOといったLLMベースFL手法が知られる。RAGとコード理解を組み合わせる流れは、GitHub CopilotのワークスペースインデックスやCursorのリポジトリ検索機能にも通じる潮流であり、コード文脈の取り扱いが品質を左右する点で共通している。

テストコード自体の障害(test smell や偽陽性)を扱う点は、プロダクションコードのFL以上に難度が高い領域であり、実務的価値も大きい可能性がある。ただし、検索精度や類似度判定の粒度によっては逆に誤誘導を生むリスクもあり、評価ベンチマークと適用範囲の妥当性が今後の議論の焦点になると見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
As LLMs are increasingly applied to software engineering tasks, this paper turns its attention to a notoriously tricky area: fault localization (FL) in test code itself. The authors propose augmenting LLM prompts with annotations derived from retrieved similar fault patterns, aiming to ground the model's reasoning in concrete prior examples rather than letting it speculate from scratch.

Traditional FL has long relied on statistical techniques such as spectrum-based (SBFL) or mutation-based (MBFL) localization, which rank suspicious statements based on test coverage and outcomes. More recent work feeds source code and failing test traces directly into an LLM, asking it to identify the offending lines in natural language. While promising, these LLM-based approaches suffer from limited context windows and hallucinated explanations, especially when the buggy logic is subtle or domain-specific.

The proposed method appears to apply a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pattern to this problem. Given a failing test or suspicious code fragment, the system retrieves semantically similar historical fault cases — likely via embedding-based nearest-neighbor search over a curated fault corpus — and injects their localized buggy regions and fix patterns as annotations into the prompt. The LLM is then expected to reason by analogy, mirroring how human developers draw on memory of past bugs when diagnosing new ones.

This line of work sits within a broader trend of combining retrieval with code understanding. Tools like GitHub Copilot's workspace indexing, Cursor's repository-wide search, and research systems such as AutoFL and LLMAO all reflect the same insight: code reasoning quality depends heavily on which surrounding context the model can see. Industrial precedents like Facebook's SapFix and Microsoft's various Copilot-driven repair features also suggest that pattern reuse from historical fixes is a powerful signal.

What makes test-code FL particularly hard, and arguably more practically valuable than it first appears, is that test failures are not always caused by production bugs. They may stem from flaky tests, test smells, brittle assertions, or environment issues. Localizing the actual fault in such ambiguous settings requires nuanced judgment, and a retrieval layer that surfaces analogous past cases could meaningfully reduce the search space for the LLM.

That said, several caveats deserve attention. The effectiveness of the approach likely hinges on the quality and coverage of the fault-pattern corpus, the embedding model used for retrieval, and the granularity at which similarity is judged. If irrelevant or superficially similar patterns are retrieved, they could mislead the LLM rather than help — a well-documented failure mode in RAG systems generally. Evaluation methodology will therefore be critical: it remains to be seen how the technique performs across diverse projects, languages, and fault types, and whether the gains hold up against strong non-retrieval LLM baselines.

Overall, the paper contributes to a growing recognition that LLM-based program analysis benefits substantially from structured, retrieval-driven context, and that test code — long underserved by automated tooling — is a fertile target for these techniques.

entries.title: Collaborator or Assistnat? How AI Coding Agents Partition Work Across Pull Request Lifecycles
entries.titleJa: AIコーディングエージェントはプルリク作業をどう分担するか
entries.titleEn: Collaborator or Assistnat? How AI Coding Agents Partition Work Across Pull Request Lifecycles
entries.summaryJa: AIコーディングエージェントが共同作業者なのか補助者なのかを、プルリクエストのライフサイクル全体での作業分担から分析した研究。コード生成・レビュー・修正の各段階でのAIと人間の役割を定量的に検証している。
entries.summaryEn: A research study examining whether AI coding agents act as true collaborators or mere assistants by analyzing how work is partitioned between humans and AI across the full pull request lifecycle, from code generation through review and revision.
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、GitHub CopilotやClaude Code、Cursorなどに代表されるAIコーディングエージェントが、ソフトウェア開発のプルリクエスト(PR)ライフサイクル全体でどのように人間と作業を分担しているかを実証的に分析した研究である。AIが単なる補助ツール(assistant)なのか、あるいは対等な共同作業者(collaborator)として機能しているのかという問いに、データに基づいて答えようとする試みだ。

研究では、PR作成からレビュー、修正、マージに至るまでの各フェーズに着目し、AIエージェントが担う作業の種類と割合、人間の介入度合いを定量化していると見られる。コード生成のような上流工程ではAIの貢献が大きい一方、レビューや品質保証では人間の判断が依然として中心になるという傾向が示される可能性がある。

背景として、近年はGitHub Copilot WorkspaceやDevin、OpenAIのCodexエージェント、AnthropicのClaude Codeなど、自律的にPRを作成・修正できる「エージェント型」開発支援ツールが急増している。これらは従来のオートコンプリート型補完を超え、Issueの解釈からテスト実行、レビューコメントへの応答までを担うことが期待されている。一方で、生成コードの品質や責任の所在、レビュー負荷の増加といった課題も指摘されており、実プロジェクトでの役割分担を測る研究は実務的にも重要性が高い。

また、SWE-benchなどのベンチマークではエージェントの自律的問題解決能力が評価されてきたが、実際のオープンソース開発における人間との協働パターンを観察する研究はまだ限定的である。本研究のような分析は、AIエージェントを導入するチームがワークフロー設計やレビュー体制を見直す際の参考材料になり得る。今後、エージェントの能力向上に伴い「補助者から共同作業者へ」のシフトが進むかどうか、継続的な観測が求められる領域と言えるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper presents an empirical investigation into how AI coding agents share work with human developers across the entire pull request (PR) lifecycle. The central question is whether these agents function as mere assistants performing narrow, supervised tasks, or whether they are evolving into genuine collaborators capable of taking ownership of substantive portions of the development workflow.

The study appears to dissect the PR lifecycle into distinct phases such as initial code generation, review, revision in response to feedback, and final merge. By measuring the proportion of activity performed by AI agents versus humans at each stage, the authors aim to characterize where AI contributions concentrate and where human judgment remains indispensable. Preliminary intuition suggests that upstream tasks like code drafting may see heavy AI involvement, while critical review and architectural decisions still rely on human oversight, though the paper's specific findings would refine this picture.

The context for this work is the rapid proliferation of agentic coding tools over the past two years. Products like GitHub Copilot Workspace, Cursor, Cognition's Devin, Anthropic's Claude Code, and OpenAI's Codex-based agents go well beyond inline autocompletion. They can interpret issues, navigate repositories, write and run tests, open PRs, and respond to review comments with little intervention. This represents a qualitative shift from the IDE-bound assistants of just a few years ago.

However, the rise of these agents has surfaced new tensions. Reviewers report increased load from AI-generated PRs that look plausible but require careful verification. Questions of accountability, code provenance, and licensing remain unsettled. Some open source maintainers have publicly pushed back against low-quality AI submissions, while others embrace agents as force multipliers. Understanding the empirical division of labor, rather than relying on vendor claims, is therefore valuable for teams designing review policies and CI workflows around agentic contributions.

Research in this space has so far leaned heavily on synthetic benchmarks such as SWE-bench, which measure an agent's ability to solve isolated GitHub issues autonomously. While useful, these benchmarks abstract away the messy social dynamics of real collaboration: negotiation in review threads, iterative scope changes, and the implicit knowledge maintainers bring. Studies that observe agents operating in live repositories alongside humans offer a complementary, more ecologically valid view of capability and integration.

The collaborator-versus-assistant framing is more than rhetorical. If agents are merely assistants, existing code review and authorship conventions largely suffice, with the human signing the commit retaining full responsibility. If they are collaborators, projects may need new conventions for attributing work, gating merges, and evaluating performance. Some organizations have begun experimenting with bot accounts that explicitly mark agent-authored PRs, while others integrate agents under human identities, blurring the line.

Readers considering adoption of coding agents in their own teams may find such lifecycle-level analyses helpful for calibrating expectations. Rather than asking whether an agent can solve a benchmark task, the more practical question is which portions of a team's existing workflow it can absorb and which still demand human attention. As model capabilities continue to improve, the partition observed today is likely to shift, and longitudinal studies tracking that movement could become an important subfield of empirical software engineering research.

entries.title: Traffic Scenario Orchestration from Language via Constraint Satisfaction
entries.titleJa: 自然言語から制約充足で交通シナリオを自動生成する手法
entries.titleEn: Traffic Scenario Orchestration from Language via Constraint Satisfaction
entries.summaryJa: 自然言語による記述から自動運転テスト用の交通シナリオを生成する研究。制約充足問題として定式化し、言語モデルの解釈結果を物理的・論理的制約に変換することで、再現性と多様性の両立を狙う。
entries.summaryEn: A research paper proposing to orchestrate traffic scenarios for autonomous driving testing from natural language descriptions, by mapping language model outputs to a constraint satisfaction formulation that enforces physical and logical feasibility.
entries.bodyJa:
自動運転システムの安全性検証では、現実には稀だが致命的な交通シナリオを大量に作り出す必要がある。本論文はそのシナリオ生成を、自然言語による記述から自動化する枠組みを提案する。

基本的なアイデアは、ユーザーが「交差点で歩行者が突然飛び出し、対向車が黄信号で進入する」といった自由記述を与えると、言語モデルがそれをシーンの要素(車両数、位置、速度、軌道、信号状態など)に分解し、これを制約充足問題 (CSP) として定式化することにある。道路形状や物理法則、衝突発生の有無といった条件を制約として明示することで、言語モデル単独では避けにくい物理的非整合や論理矛盾を抑制し、所望の性質を満たすシナリオのみを解として得る狙いと見られる。

背景には、CARLA や LGSVL、NVIDIA DRIVE Sim などのシミュレータと、Scenic、OpenSCENARIO といったシナリオ記述言語の普及がある。これらは表現力が高い一方で、テストエンジニアが手で書く負荷は大きく、近年は LLM によるシナリオ DSL の自動生成研究が活発化している。ただし LLM の出力は道路上に車を浮かせる、速度が矛盾するといった不整合を含みやすく、後段のソルバや形式制約との組み合わせが鍵だとされる。

本研究の位置づけは、その「LLM + 制約ソルバ」路線の一例と考えられる。言語からの抽出層と、CSP/SMT 的な探索層を分離することで、シナリオの多様性 (言語の柔軟さ) と妥当性 (制約による保証) の両立を狙う設計と読める。応用としては、回帰テスト用コーパスの拡充、エッジケース探索、規制当局向けの説明可能なテストケース生成などが想定されよう。

一方で、自然言語の曖昧さをどこまで制約として落とし込めるか、解空間が広い場合のスケーラビリティ、生成シナリオが実世界分布をどれだけ代表するかといった課題は依然として残る。arXiv 上の研究段階のため、実装公開や他フレームワークとの比較ベンチマークが今後の評価軸になる可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Safety validation of autonomous driving systems hinges on exposing the stack to a large and diverse set of traffic scenarios, including rare but safety-critical situations that are hard to collect from real-world driving logs. This paper proposes a pipeline that turns free-form natural language descriptions into executable traffic scenarios by routing them through a constraint satisfaction formulation.

The core idea is to let a user describe a situation in plain language, such as a pedestrian suddenly crossing an intersection while an oncoming vehicle enters on a yellow light. A language model parses this description into structured scene elements: number and type of agents, initial poses, velocities, trajectories, and traffic light states. These elements are then encoded as variables in a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP), where road geometry, kinematic feasibility, timing relationships, and collision or near-miss conditions are expressed as explicit constraints. Only assignments that satisfy all constraints are emitted as valid scenarios, which the authors argue mitigates the physical and logical inconsistencies that pure LLM generation tends to produce.

This work sits within a fast-growing ecosystem around scenario-based testing. Simulators like CARLA, LGSVL and NVIDIA DRIVE Sim, together with description formats such as Scenic and OpenSCENARIO, give engineers expressive but verbose tools for authoring driving tests. Writing those scenarios by hand is tedious, so several recent efforts have explored using LLMs to synthesize scenario DSL code directly. A recurring problem is that LLM outputs may place vehicles off the road, contradict their own speeds, or describe events that violate basic dynamics. Combining language interpretation with a solver-backed constraint layer is increasingly seen as a practical mitigation.

The contribution here can be read as one instance of that LLM-plus-solver pattern. By cleanly separating a language understanding stage from a CSP search stage, the approach aims to keep the flexibility of natural language input while guaranteeing that emitted scenarios satisfy a specified set of properties. Plausible applications include expanding regression test suites for AD stacks, exploring edge cases around specific maneuvers, and producing explainable, auditable test cases for regulators who increasingly demand evidence of coverage.

Several open questions are likely to shape how useful the method becomes in practice. Natural language is ambiguous, and how completely the system can lift soft intent into hard constraints will depend on the chosen ontology and prompt design. Scalability is another concern: CSPs over many agents, long horizons, and continuous variables can become expensive, and the paper would need to demonstrate that solving remains tractable for realistic intersection or highway scenes. There is also a representativeness question, namely whether language-driven scenarios cover the operational design domain in a way that meaningfully reduces residual risk, or whether they merely produce visually plausible but statistically biased samples.

As an arXiv preprint, the work is best read as a design proposal whose value will become clearer once code, benchmarks, and head-to-head comparisons with Scenic-based or pure-LLM baselines are available. If the constraint layer proves robust, the approach could complement existing scenario libraries rather than replace them, serving as a natural language frontend to tools that safety engineers already use.

entries.title: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability
entries.titleJa: コンピュータ操作AIエージェントの安全性確保:統合アーキテクチャ・ライフサイクル枠組み
entries.titleEn: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はGUIを操作するコンピュータ使用エージェント(CUA)のセキュリティ課題を整理し、アーキテクチャとライフサイクルを統合した信頼性フレームワークを提案する。デプロイ現場での脅威モデルや緩和策を体系化し、実運用に根ざした評価軸を示す。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a unified architecture-lifecycle framework for securing computer-use agents (CUAs) that operate GUIs, organizing threats and mitigations grounded in real deployment to improve reliability across the full agent lifecycle.
entries.bodyJa:
画面を見てマウスやキーボードを操作する「コンピュータ使用エージェント(Computer-Use Agent, CUA)」が急速に実用段階へ入りつつある中、本論文はその安全性と信頼性を体系的に扱う統合フレームワークを提示している。

著者らはCUA特有のリスクを、モデル層・エージェント層・環境層といったアーキテクチャ的視点と、設計・学習・評価・運用・廃止というライフサイクル的視点の二軸で整理する。プロンプトインジェクションや画面要素を介した間接攻撃、誤クリックによる不可逆操作、認証情報の漏洩、サンドボックス外への副作用など、CUAに固有の脅威を網羅的にマッピングし、緩和策を各段階に紐づけて議論しているとみられる。

背景として、Anthropic の Claude Computer Use、OpenAI の Operator、Google の Project Mariner など、主要ベンダーがブラウザやデスクトップを直接操作するエージェントを相次いで投入しており、評価ベンチマークも OSWorld や WebArena、AgentBench などが整備されつつある。一方で、これらは能力評価が中心で、セキュリティ評価は断片的との指摘も多い。本論文の「デプロイ接地(deployment-grounded)」というキーワードは、実環境での副作用や権限境界を前提に信頼性を測ろうという姿勢を反映していると読める。

関連分野としては、LLMエージェントの一般的なガードレール研究、RPA(ロボティック・プロセス・オートメーション)におけるアクセス制御や監査ログ、ブラウザ拡張のサンドボックス設計などが参考になる。CUAはこれらの中間的存在であり、汎用的なAI推論と機械的な自動化の両面を併せ持つため、従来手法の単純な転用では不十分な可能性がある。

本論文は具体的な実装よりも統合的なリファレンス枠組みの提示に重心があると見られ、今後の標準化や監査基準の議論の出発点として参照される可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
As computer-use agents (CUAs) — AI systems that perceive screens and drive mice and keyboards like a human operator — move from demos toward real deployments, this paper attempts to give the field a coherent way of reasoning about their security and reliability. Rather than focusing on a single attack class, it proposes a unified framework that crosses both architectural layers and the agent lifecycle.

On the architecture axis, the authors appear to decompose a CUA into the underlying model, the agent orchestration layer (planning, memory, tool use), and the surrounding environment (operating system, browser, applications, network). Each layer surfaces distinct risks: model-level issues such as prompt injection and jailbreaks; agent-level issues such as unsafe tool composition, runaway loops, or credential mishandling; and environment-level issues such as escaping sandboxes or producing irreversible side effects on real user data.

On the lifecycle axis, the framework spans design, training and fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning. The point is that security cannot be bolted on at inference time alone — for example, red-teaming during evaluation must reflect the same GUI surfaces and permissions the agent will actually encounter in production, and monitoring must capture not just text outputs but pixel-level actions and their downstream effects.

The "deployment-grounded" framing is notable. Much of the existing CUA literature, including benchmarks like OSWorld, WebArena, VisualWebArena and AgentBench, has concentrated on task success rates. Security work, by contrast, has often been fragmented across indirect prompt injection studies, browser-agent attack demos, and general LLM guardrail research. By insisting that reliability claims be tied to concrete deployment contexts — what the agent can touch, what is reversible, what is auditable — the paper pushes toward a more operational notion of trust.

The broader ecosystem context matters here. Anthropic's Claude Computer Use, OpenAI's Operator, and Google's Project Mariner have each shipped agents that drive real interfaces, and Microsoft and several startups are pursuing similar directions for enterprise automation. These systems sit between classical RPA, where actions are scripted and access is tightly scoped, and open-ended LLM agents, where reasoning is flexible but boundaries are fuzzy. Lessons from RPA governance (least privilege, audit trails, human approval for sensitive steps) and from browser extension security (capability isolation, origin boundaries) are likely to inform CUA hardening, though direct transfer may be insufficient given the probabilistic nature of model-driven control.

The paper appears more oriented toward establishing a reference framework than toward proposing a single new defense mechanism. That makes it potentially useful as scaffolding for future standards, audit checklists, or regulatory discussions around autonomous desktop and web agents. Readers should treat the taxonomy as a starting structure rather than a finished solution; empirical validation across diverse deployments will likely be needed before any specific recommendation can be considered settled.

entries.title: Search-based Robustness Testing of Laptop Refurbishing Robotic Software
entries.titleJa: ノートPC再生ロボットソフトの探索的ロバストネステスト
entries.titleEn: Search-based Robustness Testing of Laptop Refurbishing Robotic Software
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、ノートPCを分解・再生する協働ロボットの制御ソフトウェアに対し、探索ベースのテスト手法を用いて環境ばらつきへの堅牢性を評価する手法を提案する。シミュレーション上で外乱条件を最適化探索し、故障につながる入力組合せを効率的に発見する。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a search-based robustness testing approach for robotic software that disassembles and refurbishes used laptops, using simulation and optimization to discover environmental perturbations that lead to task failures.
entries.bodyJa:
使用済みノートPCの再生・解体を自動化する協働ロボットは、循環型経済を支える有望な応用領域だが、対象となるPC個体の形状ばらつきや部品配置の差異が大きく、ソフトウェアの堅牢性確保が課題となる。本論文は、こうした再生用ロボットソフトウェアに対し、探索ベース(search-based)のロバストネステスト手法を適用した研究である。

提案手法では、シミュレーション環境内でロボットがネジ外しや部品取り出しといったタスクを実行する際の入力条件、たとえば部品位置の誤差、摩擦係数、照明条件、センサーノイズなどをパラメータ化し、進化的アルゴリズムなどのメタヒューリスティクスでロバストネスを最も損なう組合せを探索する。これにより、人手では網羅が困難な境界条件や失敗ケースを効率的に同定でき、テスト工数の削減と信頼性向上を狙う。

背景として、自律システムや産業用ロボットの検証では、すべての物理状況を実機で再現することが非現実的であるため、シミュレーションと探索的テストを組み合わせるアプローチが近年広がっている。自動運転分野ではWaymoやIntel配下のMobileyeが類似のシナリオ生成・敵対的テストを実用化しており、ロボティクス向けでもGazeboやNVIDIA Isaac Simといったプラットフォーム上でフォールトインジェクションを行う研究が増えている。本研究はその系譜を再生産業という比較的新しい応用に拡張するものと位置付けられる。

EUを中心に電子廃棄物削減と修理権(Right to Repair)の議論が進む中、ノートPC再生の自動化はビジネス的にも政策的にも注目度が高い。一方で、対象機体の世代差や設計の非統一性が壁となるため、ロボット側ソフトウェアの「未知への耐性」を定量的に検証する手法は今後さらに重要性を増す可能性がある。本論文の探索ベース手法は、その評価基盤の一部を担うものと見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
Refurbishing and disassembling used laptops with collaborative robots is an increasingly attractive application in the circular economy, but the wide variability of devices, components, and physical conditions makes software robustness a critical challenge. This paper investigates that problem by applying search-based robustness testing to the control software of a laptop-refurbishing robot.

The core idea is to model environmental and task-level perturbations, such as small offsets in component positions, friction coefficients, lighting and sensor noise, or geometric variation between laptop models, as a parameter space. Metaheuristic search techniques, typically evolutionary algorithms, then explore this space inside a simulator to find input combinations that most degrade the robot's performance or cause outright failure during operations like unscrewing or part extraction. Compared to manual scenario design, this approach can uncover edge cases that human testers would likely overlook and provides quantitative insight into where the system's robustness boundaries lie.

The approach fits into a broader trend in autonomous-systems engineering. Validating robots or self-driving stacks purely with physical trials is impractical, so the community has been combining high-fidelity simulation with adversarial or search-based scenario generation. Autonomous-driving teams such as Waymo and Mobileye have publicised similar falsification pipelines, and in robotics, simulators like Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and MuJoCo are increasingly paired with fault-injection or coverage-driven testing frameworks. Academic work on search-based software testing, going back to tools like EvoSuite for unit tests, has gradually expanded into cyber-physical and AI-enabled systems, where the oracle problem and continuous input spaces make traditional testing techniques insufficient.

What makes the laptop-refurbishing context distinctive is the extreme heterogeneity of the work pieces. Unlike a factory line producing identical units, a refurbishing cell receives laptops from many vendors and generations, with different screw layouts, hinge mechanics and internal arrangements. Vision and manipulation pipelines therefore must tolerate not only sensor noise but also structural surprises. By systematically searching for perturbations that break task execution in simulation, developers can prioritise which perception modules, grasp strategies or motion-planning parameters need hardening before deployment, and can build regression suites that guard against reintroducing known weaknesses.

There is also a policy dimension worth noting. The European Union's push on electronic waste reduction and the Right to Repair movement is creating economic incentives to automate device refurbishment at scale. If such robotic cells are to operate reliably with limited human supervision, demonstrable robustness becomes a prerequisite, both for safety and for business viability. Techniques like the one described in this paper may form part of the verification toolchain that future certification or quality-assurance regimes rely on, although it is too early to say how standardised such practices will become.

Readers should treat the work as a research contribution rather than a finished industrial methodology. Search-based testing inherently depends on the fidelity of the simulator and the chosen fitness functions, and results obtained in simulation do not automatically transfer to physical hardware. Still, by targeting a concrete and socially relevant application, the study illustrates how software engineering research on robustness can move beyond generic benchmarks toward the messy realities of real-world robotics.

entries.title: Can I Check What I Designed? Mapping Security Design DSLs to Code Analyzers
entries.titleJa: セキュリティ設計DSLとコード解析ツールの対応付け手法
entries.titleEn: Can I Check What I Designed? Mapping Security Design DSLs to Code Analyzers
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、セキュアバイデザインを支援するため、セキュリティ設計DSLで記述された設計上の意図を、実装段階のコード解析ツールに対応付ける手法を提案する。設計と実装の乖離を埋め、設計時のセキュリティ要件が実装で守られているかを自動検証する枠組みを示している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes an approach to map security design DSLs onto code analyzers, bridging the gap between secure-by-design specifications and implementation-level verification so that design intent can be automatically checked against the actual code.
entries.bodyJa:
ソフトウェアのセキュアバイデザインを実現するうえで、設計段階で表明されたセキュリティ上の意図が、実装段階で実際に守られているかを確認する手段は長年の課題である。本論文は、セキュリティ設計を表現するドメイン特化言語 (DSL) と、実装コードを検査する静的解析ツールとの間の対応関係を体系的に構築する手法を提案している。

著者らは、設計DSLで記述された制約(例えば認証境界、データフローの分離、暗号化対象、信頼境界など)を、既存のコード解析ツールが検出可能なルールやクエリへ変換することを試みている。これにより、設計者が「こう守られるべき」と書いた事項について、開発者が実装段階で対応する解析を自動的に走らせ、整合性を検証できるようになると見られる。

背景として、Microsoft の脅威モデリングツールや OWASP の Threat Dragon といった設計支援ツールは普及している一方、それらの出力は実装の検証と切り離されがちであった。また CodeQL、Semgrep、SonarQube のようなコード解析ツールは強力だが、設計者の意図とは独立したルールセットを用いるため、設計と実装の追跡性が確保しづらい。本研究はその橋渡しを狙っており、いわゆる DevSecOps パイプラインで設計成果物を継続的に検証可能にする方向性に位置づけられる可能性がある。

一方で、設計レベルの抽象概念をコードレベルの構文パターンへ正確に落とし込むことは容易ではなく、対応付けの網羅性や偽陽性・偽陰性の扱いは今後の評価課題と考えられる。設計の形式性を高める方向と、解析ツール側に意味情報を付与する方向の双方が研究コミュニティで議論されており、本論文はその一例として位置づけられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Ensuring that the security properties promised at design time actually hold in the resulting implementation has long been a difficult problem in secure software engineering. This paper tackles that gap by proposing a systematic way to map constructs from a security design DSL onto the rules and queries supported by existing source code analyzers.

The central idea is that when a designer expresses concerns such as trust boundaries, authentication checkpoints, data flow restrictions, or fields that must be encrypted, those high-level statements should be translated into concrete checks that a static analysis tool can execute against the codebase. By formalising this translation, the authors aim to give teams a way to continuously verify that the implementation does not silently drift away from the intended security architecture.

The motivation is grounded in a familiar disconnect in industry practice. Threat modelling tools such as Microsoft's Threat Modeling Tool or OWASP Threat Dragon help teams articulate risks early, but their artefacts rarely feed back into the build pipeline. Conversely, analyzers like CodeQL, Semgrep, or SonarQube are powerful but typically operate from their own generic rule sets, with little traceability to the original design decisions. Bridging the two could make secure-by-design more than a slogan, and it fits naturally into the broader DevSecOps trend of shifting verification earlier and automating it.

Technically, the approach appears to rely on identifying patterns in the DSL that correspond to detectable code-level signatures. For instance, a declared trust boundary might be mapped to taint-tracking queries that flag unsanitised flows crossing it, while a confidentiality annotation on a data element could translate into checks that the corresponding field is never logged or serialised in plain form. The viability of such mappings depends heavily on how precisely the DSL captures semantics that the analyzer can recognise, and how the analyzer is configured for the target language and framework.

Several caveats are worth noting. Translating abstract design intent into syntactic or even semantic code patterns is inherently lossy, and false positives or missed detections are likely to remain a practical concern. The completeness of the mapping, its portability across analyzers, and the cost of maintaining it as code evolves are open questions that empirical evaluation will need to address. There is also a longer-running debate in the research community about whether to push the design language toward greater formality or to enrich analyzers with more semantic context; this work can be read as a pragmatic middle path that leverages tools teams already use.

If the approach matures, it could complement emerging efforts around software bills of materials, policy-as-code, and architecture conformance checking, all of which share the goal of making non-functional properties continuously auditable. For practitioners, the most immediate value may lie not in full automation but in having an explicit, machine-readable link between design artefacts and the specific analyzer rules that justify each security claim.

entries.title: Assessing, Exploiting, and Mitigating Syntactic Robustness Failures in LLM-Based Code Generation
entries.titleJa: LLMコード生成における構文ロバスト性の評価と緩和
entries.titleEn: Assessing, Exploiting, and Mitigating Syntactic Robustness Failures in LLM-Based Code Generation
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はLLMによるコード生成が、機能的に等価な自然言語プロンプトの言い換えに対して脆弱である問題を扱う。著者らは構文的揺らぎでの失敗率を評価し、攻撃手法を提示するとともに、プロンプト正規化による緩和策を提案している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper evaluates how LLM-based code generators fail when prompts are paraphrased into semantically equivalent variants, demonstrates exploitation strategies, and proposes mitigation techniques based on prompt normalization to improve syntactic robustness.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を用いたコード生成は、GitHub CopilotやChatGPTの普及により実務開発に深く浸透した。一方で、同じ意図を表す自然言語プロンプトでも、言い回しがわずかに変わるだけで生成コードの正答率が大きく揺らぐ「構文ロバスト性」の問題が指摘されている。本論文はこの問題を体系的に評価し、攻撃と緩和の両側面から検討したものである。

著者らはまず、機能的に等価な複数のプロンプト言い換え(パラフレーズ)を生成し、複数のLLMコード生成器に与えて出力の正答率を比較する評価フレームワークを構築している。実験では、語順変更や同義語置換といった意味を保つ変形であっても、テスト通過率が顕著に低下するケースが観測されたとされる。これは、モデルが入力の表層的パターンに依存していることを示唆する。

さらに著者らは、この脆弱性を意図的に突く攻撃手法を提示する。最小限の言い換えで生成失敗を誘発する敵対的プロンプトを構築できることを示し、コード生成サービスの信頼性に対するリスクを浮き彫りにした。

緩和策として提案されているのは、推論前にプロンプトを正規化(canonicalize)するアプローチである。多様な言い換えを同一の標準形に写像することで、モデルが揺らぎに左右されにくくなると論じている。実装上は前処理レイヤとして既存パイプラインに挿入できる点が利点と見られる。

関連する研究領域として、自然言語処理におけるパラフレーズ頑健性、敵対的入力に対するNLPモデルの脆弱性、コード生成評価指標としてのHumanEvalやMBPPなどが挙げられる。最近はAmazon CodeWhispererやGoogleのコード生成研究でもプロンプトエンジニアリングと評価の厳密化が進んでおり、本研究のような構文ロバスト性の体系的検証は、実運用の品質保証においても重要性を増す可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Code generation with large language models has become a daily tool for developers thanks to GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT and similar assistants. Yet a subtle reliability concern keeps surfacing: two natural language prompts that mean exactly the same thing can produce dramatically different code, with one passing all tests and the other failing outright. This paper studies that phenomenon, which the authors frame as syntactic robustness, and investigates it from three angles: assessment, exploitation, and mitigation.

The authors construct an evaluation pipeline that generates semantically equivalent paraphrases of coding prompts and feeds them to several LLM-based code generators. By comparing pass rates across paraphrases of the same task, they quantify how brittle current systems are to surface-level rewording. The reported findings indicate that even innocuous changes such as reordering clauses or substituting synonyms can meaningfully degrade functional correctness, suggesting that the models rely on shallow lexical cues more than one might expect from systems that appear fluent.

Building on the assessment, the paper turns adversarial. The authors describe how an attacker, or simply a careless user, can deliberately craft minimal paraphrases that drive the model toward incorrect or non-compiling output. This exploitation angle matters because code generators are increasingly embedded in IDEs and CI pipelines where small reliability gaps can translate into real defects or supply-chain style risks.

For mitigation, the work proposes normalizing prompts before they reach the model. The idea is to map the many possible phrasings of a request into a canonical form, so the generator sees a consistent input regardless of how the human originally expressed it. Such a preprocessing layer could in principle be added to existing toolchains without retraining the underlying model, which would make adoption relatively cheap, though the effectiveness likely depends on the quality and coverage of the normalization step.

The broader context is worth noting. Robustness to paraphrase has long been studied in NLP, including adversarial attacks on classifiers and question answering systems, but code generation raises the stakes because outputs are executable. Benchmarks like HumanEval and MBPP measure functional correctness on fixed prompts, and recent variants such as HumanEval+ and EvalPlus have already begun probing how sensitive models are to test rigor and prompt variation. Industry efforts from vendors including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Amazon increasingly emphasize evaluation harnesses, and prompt engineering guides implicitly acknowledge that wording matters more than it should.

The paper's contribution sits naturally in this lineage. It does not claim to solve robustness wholesale, and the normalization-based defense may face limits when paraphrases drift far from training distributions or when domain-specific jargon resists canonicalization. Still, by combining systematic measurement, an explicit attack model, and a concrete mitigation, the work offers a useful template for hardening LLM-based developer tools as they move deeper into production environments.

entries.title: EXPEREPAIR: Dual-Memory Enhanced LLM-based Repository-Level Program Repair
entries.titleJa: EXPEREPAIR: 二重記憶でLLMによるリポジトリ規模のバグ修正を強化
entries.titleEn: EXPEREPAIR: Dual-Memory Enhanced LLM-based Repository-Level Program Repair
entries.summaryJa: EXPEREPAIRは、人間の記憶モデルに着想を得た二重メモリ機構を導入し、LLMによるリポジトリレベルの自動バグ修正能力を向上させる手法。過去の修正経験を継続的に蓄積・活用することで、SWE-bench等のベンチマークで既存手法を上回る成果を示した。
entries.summaryEn: EXPEREPAIR proposes a dual-memory architecture inspired by human cognition that continuously accumulates and reuses past bug-fixing experiences, enabling LLMs to outperform prior approaches on repository-level program repair benchmarks like SWE-bench.
entries.bodyJa:
EXPEREPAIRは、LLMを用いたリポジトリ規模の自動プログラム修正(APR)に、人間の記憶モデルに着想を得た二重メモリ機構を組み込んだ新しい手法である。複雑な実プロジェクトのバグ修正は依然として難題であり、本研究はLLMが過去の経験から学習し続ける仕組みを与えることでこの壁に挑む。

従来のLLMベースAPR手法は、各バグを独立に扱い、過去の修正事例から得られる知見を活用しない傾向にあった。EXPEREPAIRはこれに対し、短期記憶と長期記憶に相当する二層構造を導入する。短期記憶は直近の修正過程における中間情報を保持し、長期記憶は過去に解決したバグから抽出した一般化可能な修正パターンや戦略を蓄積する。新たなバグに遭遇した際、関連する経験を検索・参照することで、より精度の高い修正候補生成が可能になるとされる。

評価はリポジトリレベルAPRのデファクト標準であるSWE-benchなどのベンチマークで行われ、既存のエージェント型・非エージェント型手法を上回る修正成功率を示したと報告されている。経験の蓄積が増えるほど性能が向上する傾向も示唆されており、継続学習的な側面が魅力的である。

背景として、リポジトリレベルAPRは2023年以降のSWE-benchの登場で急速に注目を集め、SWE-agent、AutoCodeRover、Agentlessなど多様なアプローチが提案されてきた。多くは検索拡張や複数エージェント協調に注力するが、過去事例の体系的な再利用は手薄だった。人間の認知科学における作業記憶と長期記憶の区分をAIエージェントに応用するアイデア自体は、Generative AgentsやMemGPTなど他分野でも見られ、APRに本格的に持ち込んだ点が本論文の位置づけと言えるだろう。

実運用面では、メモリの肥大化や不適切な事例参照によるノイズ混入が課題になり得るが、適切な抽象化と検索機構が機能すれば、長期的に成長するバグ修正アシスタントの実現に近づく可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
EXPEREPAIR introduces a dual-memory architecture, inspired by human cognitive models of working and long-term memory, to enhance LLM-based repository-level automated program repair (APR). The work targets one of the harder open problems in software engineering automation: fixing real bugs across large, interdependent codebases.

Most existing LLM-based APR pipelines treat each bug in isolation. They retrieve relevant code, prompt a model, and iterate, but they rarely retain or reuse what was learned from previously solved issues. EXPEREPAIR argues that this stateless behavior wastes a valuable signal. By emulating the dual-process structure of human memory, the system maintains a short-term memory that tracks intermediate reasoning and context during a current repair session, alongside a long-term memory that accumulates distilled fix patterns, strategies, and lessons from past bugs. When a new issue arrives, relevant experiences are retrieved and injected into the prompt, guiding patch generation toward solutions that worked in analogous situations.

The authors evaluate the approach on SWE-bench, which has become the de facto benchmark for repository-level APR since its release. They report that EXPEREPAIR outperforms prior agentic and non-agentic baselines, and that performance tends to improve as the experience pool grows, hinting at a form of continual learning without weight updates.

Contextually, repository-level APR has exploded as a research area, with systems such as SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover, and Agentless exploring different points in the design space, from heavy multi-agent orchestration to deliberately minimal pipelines. Most of these focus on better retrieval, planning, or tool use. Systematic reuse of past repair experiences has been comparatively underexplored, even though the broader agent community, with projects like Generative Agents and MemGPT, has shown that explicit memory layers can meaningfully change agent behavior. EXPEREPAIR can be read as importing those ideas into the APR setting in a principled way.

There are open questions that the paper will need to address as the line of work matures. Memory growth could become a liability if irrelevant or misleading past cases are retrieved, and the quality of the abstraction step that turns raw fix traces into reusable knowledge is likely critical. The benchmark itself has known limitations, including potential contamination with model training data, so cross-validation on newer or private benchmarks would strengthen the claims. Still, if the dual-memory design proves robust, it points toward APR assistants that genuinely improve with deployment time rather than plateauing after the initial prompt is tuned, which would be a meaningful shift for practical developer tooling.

entries.title: "Show Me You Comply... Without Showing Me Anything": Zero-Knowledge Software Auditing for AI-Enabled Systems
entries.titleJa: ゼロ知識証明でAIシステムのコンプライアンスを開示なく監査
entries.titleEn: "Show Me You Comply... Without Showing Me Anything": Zero-Knowledge Software Auditing for AI-Enabled Systems
entries.summaryJa: 本論文はAI搭載システムのソフトウェア監査にゼロ知識証明を応用し、ソースコードやモデル内部を開示せずに規制遵守を検証する手法を提案する。EU AI Actなどの規制対応とIP保護の両立を狙う。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes applying zero-knowledge proofs to software auditing of AI-enabled systems, enabling vendors to prove regulatory compliance without disclosing source code, model weights, or training data to auditors.
entries.bodyJa:
AI搭載システムへの規制圧力が高まる中、ベンダーがソースコードやモデル内部を開示せずにコンプライアンスを証明できるかが課題となっている。本論文は、暗号学的手法であるゼロ知識証明(ZKP)をソフトウェア監査に応用し、この相反する要求を両立させる枠組みを提案する。

ゼロ知識証明は、ある命題が真であることを、その命題以外の情報を一切漏らさずに検証者へ示せる暗号プロトコルである。本研究ではこれを応用し、AIシステムが特定のテストに合格していること、所定のデータセットで学習されたこと、あるいはバイアス指標が一定閾値以下であることなどを、モデル重みや訓練データ、ソースコードを開示せずに監査人へ証明する方式を検討していると見られる。

背景には、EU AI Actや米国大統領令、各国のAIガバナンス枠組みなど、AIシステムの透明性と説明責任を要求する規制の世界的な進展がある。一方でモデルや学習データは企業の重要な知的財産であり、開示は競争力やセキュリティを損なう懸念がある。さらに、第三者監査人が機微情報を扱うこと自体が新たな漏洩リスクを生むという指摘もある。

関連領域では、機械学習推論をZKPで検証するzkMLが急速に発展しており、Modulus LabsやEZKL、Giza等のプロジェクトが知られる。これらは主にオンチェーン用途を想定するが、企業内コンプライアンスや規制対応への応用は新しい潮流と位置づけられる。計算コストや回路化の難しさが実用化の障壁として残るが、ハードウェア対応の進展で改善する可能性がある。本論文はソフトウェア工学の観点から、こうした暗号技術と従来の監査プロセスを接続する設計上の論点を整理する試みと考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
As regulators worldwide tighten oversight of AI-enabled systems, vendors face an awkward dilemma: how do you prove compliance to an auditor without handing over the very assets that make your product valuable? This paper explores applying zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) to software auditing as a way to reconcile these competing demands.

Zero-knowledge proofs are cryptographic protocols that allow a prover to convince a verifier that a statement is true while revealing nothing beyond the truth of the statement itself. In the auditing context, this means a vendor could demonstrate that its AI system passed specified test suites, was trained on a sanctioned dataset, or that its bias metrics fall below regulatory thresholds, all without exposing model weights, training data, or proprietary source code to the auditor.

The motivation is timely. The EU AI Act, recent U.S. executive orders, and emerging national AI governance frameworks increasingly demand transparency, traceability, and accountability from high-risk AI systems. Yet models, training corpora, and pipelines are often core intellectual property whose disclosure could erode competitive advantage or create new security exposure. Third-party auditors themselves become attack surfaces when they hold sensitive artifacts, an issue that has surfaced in financial and security audits historically.

The approach sits at an interesting crossroads of software engineering and applied cryptography. A growing ecosystem around zero-knowledge machine learning, often called zkML, has produced tooling such as EZKL, Modulus Labs, and Giza, primarily aimed at on-chain verifiable inference. Extending these primitives from single-inference verification to broader audit obligations, covering software processes, data provenance, and continuous compliance, is a substantially harder design problem that this work appears to engage with.

Several challenges deserve hedged commentary. Generating ZKPs for large neural networks remains computationally expensive, and expressing complex audit predicates as arithmetic circuits is non-trivial. Performance is improving with specialized proof systems and hardware acceleration, but practical, end-to-end zero-knowledge audits for industrial-scale AI systems are likely still some way off. There are also governance questions: who specifies the audit predicates, and how do regulators gain confidence that the compiled circuit truly encodes the intended legal requirement?

If successful, frameworks like the one outlined here could reshape how compliance is demonstrated, shifting it from document-heavy disclosure regimes to cryptographically verifiable attestations. That would echo broader movements in privacy-preserving computation, including confidential computing enclaves and secure multiparty computation, which similarly aim to let parties cooperate on sensitive data without trusting one another fully. Whether ZKPs become the dominant mechanism or one tool among several will likely depend on tooling maturity, regulator acceptance, and the willingness of vendors to invest in non-trivial cryptographic engineering.

entries.title: Can Language Models Go Beyond Coding? Assessing the Capability of Language Models to Build Real-World Systems
entries.titleJa: 言語モデルは実世界システムを構築できるか、能力を評価する新ベンチマーク
entries.titleEn: Can Language Models Go Beyond Coding? Assessing the Capability of Language Models to Build Real-World Systems
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル(LLM)がコード生成を超えて実世界の複雑なシステムを構築できるかを評価する新たな枠組みを提案する。複数の要件を統合した実用システムの構築タスクを通じ、現行モデルの限界と課題を明らかにする。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a new benchmark to assess whether large language models can move beyond isolated code generation to build real-world software systems, revealing notable limitations of current models on integrative, multi-requirement engineering tasks.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)はコーディングタスクにおいて目覚ましい性能を示してきたが、現実世界で動作する完全なソフトウェアシステムを構築できるかは依然として不明である。本論文はその問いに正面から取り組み、LLMが断片的なコード生成を超えて実用システムを設計・実装できるかを評価する新たな枠組みを提示する。

従来のコーディングベンチマーク、例えばHumanEvalやMBPPは関数単位の問題解決能力を測るものであり、実際のソフトウェア開発に求められる要件分析、モジュール設計、依存関係管理、テスト、デプロイといった一連の工程をカバーしていない。著者らはこの限界を踏まえ、複数の要件を統合し、エンドツーエンドで動作するシステムをモデルに構築させるタスクを設計したとされる。これにより、単なるスニペット生成能力ではなく、エンジニアリング能力そのものを測定することを狙う。

評価の結果、現行のLLMは個別のコード片の生成では高い精度を示す一方、複雑な依存関係を扱うアーキテクチャ設計や、長期的な一貫性を要する実装統合では性能が大きく低下する傾向が示唆される。これは、コンテキスト長や計画能力、外部ツールとの連携といった要素が依然として課題であることを示すものと見られる。

関連する動向として、SWE-benchやLiveCodeBenchのように、GitHubのIssue修正など現実の開発タスクを模した評価が近年活発になっている。さらにDevinやOpenHands、Claude Codeのようなエージェント型コーディング環境も登場しており、LLMを「コード補完」から「ソフトウェアエンジニア」へと押し上げる試みが続く。本研究はそうした流れの中で、エージェント評価の基準を一段引き上げる意義を持つ可能性がある。今後はマルチエージェント協調や長期的計画、リポジトリ全体を踏まえた推論能力の改善が鍵となるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
Large language models have demonstrated strong performance on isolated coding tasks, but whether they can build complete, working software systems for real-world use remains an open question. This paper tackles that question directly, proposing a new framework to evaluate whether LLMs can design and implement functional systems rather than merely generate code fragments.

Existing coding benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP largely measure function-level problem solving. They do not capture the broader software engineering lifecycle, which includes requirements analysis, modular design, dependency management, integration, testing, and deployment. The authors argue that this gap leaves a misleading impression of LLM capability, and they design tasks that require models to integrate multiple requirements and deliver end-to-end systems. The aim is to assess engineering competence rather than snippet-level fluency.

Results reportedly suggest that while current LLMs perform well on localized code generation, their performance degrades significantly on tasks that demand architectural reasoning, handling complex dependencies, and maintaining long-range consistency across an implementation. This pattern points to persistent challenges around context length, planning, tool use, and the ability to reason over a whole codebase, rather than a single file or function.

The work fits into a broader shift in how the community evaluates code-generating models. Benchmarks like SWE-bench and LiveCodeBench have moved toward realistic developer scenarios, such as resolving GitHub issues or handling contamination-resistant competitive programming tasks. At the same time, agentic coding environments like Devin, OpenHands, Cursor, and Claude Code are attempting to elevate LLMs from autocomplete tools into something closer to autonomous software engineers. Against this backdrop, the proposed benchmark may help raise the bar for what it means to evaluate an AI coding agent, pushing beyond patch-level accuracy toward holistic system construction.

Several practical implications follow. First, organizations adopting LLM-based development tools may want to look past leaderboard scores on classical benchmarks and consider how models perform when stitching together components, managing state, or honoring non-functional requirements such as performance and security. Second, model developers may need to invest further in techniques like long-context reasoning, retrieval over repositories, hierarchical planning, and multi-agent coordination, all of which appear central to closing the gap identified here. Finally, the framework could serve as a useful diagnostic for future frontier models, helping clarify whether scaling alone is sufficient or whether new architectures and training paradigms are required to reach genuine software engineering competence.

As with any new benchmark, broader adoption and independent replication will be important before strong conclusions can be drawn. Still, the study contributes a timely lens for examining how far LLMs have come, and how much further they may need to go before they can be trusted to build real-world systems with limited human oversight.

entries.title: Model checking of hyperproperties for high-level relational models
entries.titleJa: 高水準関係モデルにおけるハイパープロパティのモデル検査
entries.titleEn: Model checking of hyperproperties for high-level relational models
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、複数の実行トレース間の関係を表現するハイパープロパティを、Alloyのような高水準関係モデルに対して検査する手法を提案する。情報フローやセキュリティ要件の形式的検証への応用が期待される。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a model checking technique for hyperproperties over high-level relational models such as Alloy, enabling formal verification of multi-trace properties like information flow and security requirements.
entries.bodyJa:
形式手法分野における新たな研究として、高水準関係モデルに対するハイパープロパティのモデル検査手法が提案された。ハイパープロパティとは、システムの単一実行ではなく複数の実行トレース間の関係として定義される性質であり、情報フロー制御や非干渉性、観測等価性といったセキュリティ要件の表現に不可欠な概念である。

従来のLTLやCTLといった時相論理は、単一トレース上の性質しか表現できず、機密情報の漏洩有無のような「2つの実行を比較して初めて判断できる性質」を直接扱えなかった。これに対しHyperLTLやHyperCTL*といった拡張論理が提案され、トレース変数の量化により複数実行間の関係を記述可能にしてきた経緯がある。

本研究の特徴は、こうしたハイパープロパティをAlloyに代表される高水準の関係論理ベースのモデリング言語に適用する点にあると見られる。Alloyは一階関係論理と推移閉包を備えた宣言的モデリング言語で、SATソルバを背景にした有限スコープ解析により設計の整合性検査に広く用いられている。関係モデルの表現力を活かしつつハイパープロパティを扱えれば、抽象度の高い段階でのセキュリティ設計検証が可能になる可能性がある。

関連動向としては、MITのDaniel Jackson氏らによるAlloy 6での時相論理サポート追加や、HyperLTL向けモデル検査器MCHyperの研究などが挙げられる。これらと比較して本手法がどの程度のスケーラビリティと表現力を実現するかが、実応用への鍵となるだろう。形式検証コミュニティにおいて、設計段階からのセキュリティ性質検証ニーズは高まっており、関連研究の進展が注目される。
entries.bodyEn:
A new research contribution in the formal methods space proposes a model checking approach for hyperproperties expressed over high-level relational models. Hyperproperties differ fundamentally from classical trace properties in that they relate multiple execution traces rather than constraining a single one, which makes them essential for expressing security-relevant requirements such as noninterference, observational equivalence, and information-flow control.

Traditional temporal logics like LTL and CTL can only express properties of individual traces, leaving a gap for requirements that inherently compare executions, for example detecting whether confidential inputs leak into observable outputs. To address this, the community developed hyperlogics such as HyperLTL and HyperCTL*, which introduce explicit quantification over trace variables. These logics have become a standard vehicle for formalizing security policies, but their model checking is computationally challenging and most tools target low-level transition systems.

The novelty of this work appears to lie in lifting hyperproperty verification to high-level relational modeling languages, most notably those in the Alloy family. Alloy combines first-order relational logic with transitive closure and provides bounded analysis backed by SAT solvers, making it popular for early-stage design exploration. Marrying the expressive abstraction of relational models with the multi-trace reasoning of hyperlogics could allow engineers to verify security and consistency properties at the design level, well before implementation choices are fixed.

The broader context here is worth noting. Daniel Jackson's group at MIT extended Alloy with temporal operators in Alloy 6, opening the door to behavioral and dynamic reasoning within the same declarative framework. On the hyperproperty side, tools such as MCHyper and various SMT-based verifiers have demonstrated feasibility for finite-state systems, while research on relational verification and self-composition continues to expand the technique landscape. A relational-model-based approach may complement these efforts by offering a more abstract, design-oriented entry point, though the precise scalability and expressiveness trade-offs would need to be evaluated against existing tooling.

For practitioners, the practical implication, if the approach matures, is the prospect of catching subtle information-flow bugs during architectural modeling rather than after implementation. Security properties are notoriously difficult to retrofit, and shifting their verification leftward has been a recurring theme in both academic and industrial formal methods communities. Whether this particular technique gains traction will likely depend on tool support, integration with existing Alloy workflows, and demonstrated case studies on realistic systems. As hyperproperties continue to attract attention in domains ranging from cryptographic protocols to machine learning fairness, contributions that broaden the modeling vocabulary available for their specification and checking are a welcome direction.

entries.title: AI Tools in Software Development: Developer Perceptions and Usage Patterns
entries.titleJa: 開発者から見たAIツール:利用実態と認識の調査
entries.titleEn: AI Tools in Software Development: Developer Perceptions and Usage Patterns
entries.summaryJa: ソフトウェア開発におけるAIツールの利用状況と開発者の認識を調査した研究。コード生成やデバッグでの活用が広がる一方、生産性向上の実感や信頼性、品質面で評価が分かれることが示された。
entries.summaryEn: A study examining how software developers perceive and use AI tools in their daily work, revealing widespread adoption for coding and debugging but mixed views on productivity gains, trust, and output quality.
entries.bodyJa:
GitHub CopilotやChatGPTに代表される生成AIツールは、ここ数年でソフトウェア開発の現場に急速に浸透した。本論文は、開発者がそうしたAIツールをどのように使い、どう評価しているのかを調査した研究である。

調査では、コード補完、バグ修正、ドキュメント生成、テストコード作成、リファクタリング支援といった用途でAIツールが日常的に利用されている実態が示されたとされる。特に定型的なコード生成や、未知のAPI・フレームワークを学ぶ際の初期理解の補助として有用性が認識される傾向がある。一方で、生成されたコードの正確性や保守性、セキュリティ面については疑念を持つ開発者も少なくなく、利用後に必ずレビューを行うという慎重な運用が一般的と見られる。

生産性については、単純作業の時間短縮を実感する声がある一方、複雑なロジックや既存コードベース固有の文脈を扱う場面では、AIの提案を修正する手間がかえって増えるという指摘もある。また、過度な依存によるスキル低下への懸念や、ライセンス・著作権、機密コードの漏洩といった組織的リスクも論点として挙げられている。

背景として、Stack OverflowのDeveloper Surveyなど他の業界調査でも、開発者の大多数がAIコーディング支援を試用済みである一方、出力の信頼性に対する完全な信頼は限定的という同様の傾向が報告されている。GitHub Copilot、Cursor、Claude Code、Windsurfなどエージェント型ツールへと進化が進む中で、単なる補完から自律的なタスク実行へと利用形態がシフトしつつあり、本研究のような利用実態の継続的な観測は、ツール設計や組織導入方針の指針として今後も重要性を増すと考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
Generative AI tools such as GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT have rapidly become part of everyday software development over the past few years. This paper investigates how developers actually use such tools and how they perceive their value, limitations, and risks.

According to the study, AI assistants are routinely employed for a wide range of tasks: code completion, bug fixing, generating documentation, writing unit tests, and assisting with refactoring. Developers appear to find them particularly useful for boilerplate generation and for getting an initial grasp of unfamiliar APIs or frameworks. At the same time, many respondents express reservations about the correctness, maintainability, and security of generated code, and it seems common practice to subject AI suggestions to careful human review before integration.

On productivity, the picture is mixed. Some developers report tangible time savings on routine work, while others note that revising AI suggestions for complex logic or for tasks deeply tied to a specific codebase can offset, or even exceed, the time saved. Concerns about skill erosion from over-reliance, along with organizational issues such as licensing, intellectual property, and the risk of leaking confidential code into external services, also feature prominently in the discussion.

These findings echo trends observed in broader industry surveys. Stack Overflow's annual Developer Survey, for instance, has repeatedly shown that a large majority of developers have tried AI coding assistants, yet only a smaller share fully trusts their output. JetBrains and GitHub's own usage reports paint a similar picture: enthusiastic adoption tempered by caution about quality and accountability.

The ecosystem itself is evolving quickly. Beyond inline completion tools like Copilot, agentic environments such as Cursor, Windsurf, and Claude Code are pushing the model from suggestion toward more autonomous task execution, including multi-file edits and running tests. This shift may amplify both the benefits and the risks the paper highlights, since errors in autonomous workflows can propagate further before a human notices them.

For engineering organizations, studies of this kind offer useful grounding. Rather than treating AI tools as a uniformly positive productivity multiplier, the evidence suggests their impact depends heavily on task type, codebase complexity, and the maturity of review practices around them. Teams that invest in clear usage guidelines, code review discipline, and training on how to prompt and validate AI output are likely to extract more value while containing downside risks.

It should be noted that self-reported survey data, as used here, tends to capture perception rather than objective performance, and results can shift quickly as tools improve. Continuous, longitudinal observation of developer behavior — ideally combined with telemetry and controlled experiments — will likely be needed to form a durable picture of how AI is reshaping software engineering practice.

entries.title: AgenticSZZ: Temporal Knowledge Graph-Guided Agentic Bug-Inducing Commit Identification
entries.titleJa: AgenticSZZ: 時間知識グラフを活用したバグ誘発コミット特定エージェント
entries.titleEn: AgenticSZZ: Temporal Knowledge Graph-Guided Agentic Bug-Inducing Commit Identification
entries.summaryJa: AgenticSZZは、従来のSZZアルゴリズムを拡張し、時間的知識グラフとLLMエージェントを組み合わせることでバグ誘発コミットを高精度に特定する新手法である。コード履歴の文脈を動的に追跡し、誤検知の削減を狙う。
entries.summaryEn: AgenticSZZ proposes an agentic approach combining temporal knowledge graphs and LLM agents to identify bug-inducing commits more accurately, extending the classic SZZ algorithm by capturing contextual code history and reducing false positives.
entries.bodyJa:
ソフトウェア工学の分野では、バグの原因となったコミットを特定する作業はデバッグや品質管理の根幹をなす。AgenticSZZは、この古典的課題に対し、時間的知識グラフ(Temporal Knowledge Graph)とエージェント型LLMを組み合わせた新たなアプローチを提示する研究である。

従来のSZZアルゴリズム(Śliwerski、Zimmermann、Zellerらが2005年に提案)は、バグ修正コミットの差分から「以前に該当行を変更したコミット」を遡って特定する方式で広く利用されてきた。しかし、リファクタリングや単純なフォーマット変更が混入すると誤検知が増えるという課題が知られており、AG-SZZやMA-SZZ、PyDriller統合版など多数の改良版が提案されてきた経緯がある。

本論文のAgenticSZZは、コード変更履歴をノードとエッジで表現する時間的知識グラフを構築し、LLMエージェントが対話的にグラフ上を探索することで、真にバグを誘発したと考えられるコミットを推論する仕組みを取るとされる。エージェントは静的なヒューリスティクスではなく、変更の意味的文脈と時系列依存関係を踏まえて判断する点に新規性があると見られる。

背景として、近年はLLMを用いたソフトウェア工学タスクの自動化が活発で、Microsoft ResearchやMetaがバグ検出・修正にLLMエージェントを応用する研究を進めており、SWE-bench等のベンチマークも整備されつつある。SZZの精度向上は、Just-in-Timeバグ予測やセキュリティ脆弱性のライフサイクル解析に直結するため、産業界からの関心も高い分野である。

一方で、LLMエージェントによる推論はコストや再現性に課題があり、実プロジェクトの大規模リポジトリで一貫した精度を保てるかは今後の検証が必要だろう。論文の評価データセットや既存SZZ亜種との比較結果に注目したい。
entries.bodyEn:
Identifying the commit that originally introduced a bug is a foundational task in software engineering, underpinning debugging, defect prediction, and vulnerability lifecycle analysis. AgenticSZZ proposes a fresh take on this problem by marrying temporal knowledge graphs with LLM-based agents to trace bug-inducing commits with greater contextual awareness than traditional heuristics allow.

The original SZZ algorithm, introduced by Śliwerski, Zimmermann, and Zeller in 2005, works by examining the diff of a bug-fix commit and walking back through version control history to find the commit that last touched the offending lines. While simple and widely adopted, it is notoriously prone to false positives when lines were modified for cosmetic reasons, refactoring, or unrelated formatting changes. Over the years researchers have produced numerous refinements—AG-SZZ, MA-SZZ, RA-SZZ, and PyDriller-based variants—each attempting to filter out non-semantic changes.

AgenticSZZ pushes this lineage in a new direction. According to the paper, it constructs a temporal knowledge graph in which nodes and edges encode the evolution of code entities over time, and then lets an LLM agent navigate this graph to reason about which historical commit most plausibly introduced a defect. Rather than relying on static line-mapping rules, the agent appears to consider semantic context and temporal dependencies, querying the graph iteratively much like a developer would when investigating a regression.

The broader context is notable. LLM agents have rapidly become a popular tool for software engineering automation, with efforts from Microsoft Research, Meta, and various academic groups exploring autonomous debugging, patch synthesis, and code review. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench have raised the bar for what agentic systems are expected to do on real repositories. Improving SZZ accuracy directly feeds into downstream tasks like just-in-time defect prediction, CVE provenance tracing, and empirical studies of how vulnerabilities are introduced into open-source code, so industrial interest in this niche is genuine.

That said, agentic approaches come with caveats. LLM inference is expensive relative to rule-based diff analysis, and reproducibility can suffer when model behavior shifts between versions. It remains to be seen whether AgenticSZZ scales gracefully to large monorepos with deep histories, and whether its gains hold up across languages and project styles. The paper's evaluation against established SZZ variants and the choice of ground-truth datasets will likely determine how influential the approach becomes.

If the results are robust, AgenticSZZ could signal a wider trend: replacing fixed heuristics in mining software repositories with agentic reasoning over structured project histories. Temporal knowledge graphs themselves are an emerging representation in MSR research, and pairing them with LLM agents may prove a durable pattern beyond bug attribution alone.
